title: Adaptable Bodyweight Strength
goal: Explore adaptable Bodyweight Strength at a comfortable, adaptable level.
readiness: Adolescent maintains a steady bodyweight plank for 30+ seconds.
steps: Warm up with easy movement.
Choose a wall or incline push-up and a comfortable supported core movement.
Try a few controlled repetitions, breathe normally and rest before form becomes difficult.
Use a qualified instructor for unfamiliar exercises and adapt to current ability.
completionCriteria: Participant practises an adapted push or core movement with comfortable form and rest; no repetition threshold is required.
safety: Avoid lumbar hyperextension or cervical forward poked head posture.
Stop if anterior shoulder pain occurs.
adaptations: Use shorter attempts, accessible materials or additional support.
Adapt the activity to your language, interests, health and current ability; participation does not require unassisted performance.

title: Metacognitive Journaling Practice
goal: Explore metacognitive Journaling Practice at a comfortable, adaptable level.
readiness: Adolescent can reflect in writing on personal experiences.
steps: Designate a private notebook in a screen-free space.
Set a timer for 10 minutes.
Respond to 3 structured prompts: (a) 'What depleted my energy today?', (b) 'What gave me genuine energy?', (c) 'How did I respond under pressure?'.
Conclude by naming one personal value (e.g., integrity, patience, curiosity) to consciously practice the next day.
completionCriteria: Maintains a handwritten journal 4 days per week for 2 consecutive weeks, documenting structured self-evaluations.
safety: Emphasize personal privacy; journal is private to the teenager unless they choose to share.
adaptations: Use shorter attempts, accessible materials or additional support.
Adapt the activity to your language, interests, health and current ability; participation does not require unassisted performance.
benefits: Offers voluntary practice with shared attention, connection and expressing preferences or feelings.

title: Analytical Expository Writing & Source Synthesis
goal: Explore analytical Expository Writing & Source Synthesis at a comfortable, adaptable level.
readiness: Adolescent writes multi-paragraph essays and summarizes texts.
steps: Select a contemporary or historical question with differing credible perspectives.
Read and annotate two short contrasting source articles, highlighting thesis statements, data points, and potential biases.
Draft a structured 350-to-400-word expository essay featuring an introductory thesis, evidence from both sources, and a logical resolution.
Review and edit transitions to ensure cohesive flow between opposing paragraphs.
completionCriteria: Produces a written 400-word synthesis paper citing two distinct sources with a coherent thesis, evidence citations, and formal transition mechanics.
safety: Provide constructive feedback focusing on logical flow rather than subjective opinions.
adaptations: Use shorter attempts, accessible materials or additional support.
Adapt the activity to your language, interests, health and current ability; participation does not require unassisted performance.

title: Long-Horizon Project & Time Architecture
goal: Explore long-Horizon Project & Time Architecture at a comfortable, adaptable level.
steps: Identify an authentic 3-to-4-week goal (academic term paper, science fair project, or learning a creative skill).
Write the final deadline on a calendar and work backward to establish weekly milestone deliverables.
Deconstruct each week into daily, manageable 30-minute actionable tasks.
Conduct a weekly 10-minute retrospective to compare projected versus completed tasks and recalibrate accordingly.
completionCriteria: Adolescent completes a self-directed 3-week project within 3 days of original target deadline accompanied by weekly logged planning retrospectives.
safety: Encourage realistic buffer times to prevent burnout or last-minute panic.
adaptations: Use shorter attempts, accessible materials or additional support.

title: Structured Empathy & Perspective-Taking Dialogue
goal: Explore structured Empathy & Perspective-Taking Dialogue at a comfortable, adaptable level.

duration: Up to 15 minutes per planned opportunity, with breaks or shorter attempts as needed.

completionCriteria: Adolescent accurately paraphrases an opposing viewpoint to the speaker's satisfaction across 3 separate dialogue sessions without sarcasm or distortion.
steps: Choose a low-stakes topic of disagreement (e.g., household screen limits or curfew choices).
Instruct Person A to state their position for 2 minutes.
Require Person B (the adolescent) to paraphrase Person A's exact perspective until Person A confirms: 'Yes, that accurately represents my view.'
Switch roles so the adolescent practices being heard, then formulate a collaborative compromise.
